course_name_en: Modeling and Simulation of Mechanical Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Introduction to concepts of integrity and durability of structures with defects and cracks, definition of fracture mechanics parameters, and application of fracture mechanics criteria.

Analytical, numerical using specialized software, and experimental determination of fracture mechanics parameters, and familiarization with national and international standards for fracture toughness determination.

syllabus_topics: Introduction, specific elements of fracture mechanics
Linear-elastic fracture mechanics. Griffith's theory. Westergaard's solution. Irwin's approximation. Definition of the stress intensity factor
Stress intensity factor for bodies with different types of cracks
Aspects of finite element modeling of bodies with cracks. Realization of crack tip singularity. Methods for estimating fracture mechanics parameters
Experimental methods for determining the stress intensity factor
Experimental determination of fracture toughness. Factors influencing fracture toughness
Aspects of elasto-plastic fracture mechanics. Size of the plastic zone formed at the crack tip. Crack tip opening displacement. J-integral
Analytical calculation of fracture mechanics parameters in the linear-elastic domain
Calculation of crack propagation speed and durability of structural elements
Experimental determination of fracture toughness. KIC method
Determination of stress intensity factor at a crack tip by photoelasticity
Determination of crack propagation speed under variable loads
Determination of fracture mechanics parameters by the Finite Element Method
Estimation of durability of structural elements based on fracture mechanics principles
teaching_methods: Finite Element Method using specialized software

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (2 theory subjects and 1 application)
Short project performed during laboratory hours (determination of stress intensity factors by Finite Element Method)

assessment_rules: The minimum performance standard requires knowledge of linear elastic and elasto-plastic fracture mechanics parameters, assimilation and application of crack failure criteria for cracked parts, and performing numerical simulations for determining fracture mechanics parameters. Assessment criteria for lectures include knowledge of fracture mechanics terminology and assimilation of calculation methodology. Applied activities are evaluated based on presence, answers to applications, and scores from computer simulation works.
